Project accounts-api. Hidden tests import these names exactly, so keep them: app/services/counter_store.py defines class CounterStoreError(Exception); class CounterStore(Protocol) with get(key: str) -> int (0 when the key is missing or expired), incr(key: str) -> int (the new count; a new key starts at 1 with no expiry), expire(key: str, seconds: int) -> None, ttl(key: str) -> int (seconds left; -1 with no expiry, -2 when missing, as in Redis), and delete(key: str) -> None; class InMemoryCounterStore with __init__(self, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic) that honors expiry by that clock; and class RedisCounterStore with __init__(self, url: str) that imports redis inside __init__ and turns every redis.exceptions.RedisError into CounterStoreError.

app/services/users.py: @dataclass(frozen=True) class User with id: int, email: str, password_hash: str; class UserRepository(Protocol) with get_by_email(email: str) -> User | None; class InMemoryUserRepository with __init__(self, users: Iterable[User] = ()). app/services/passwords.py: hash_password(password: str, *, salt: bytes | None = None) -> str and verify_password(password: str, password_hash: str) -> bool, with hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac and hmac.compare_digest.

app/services/auth.py: def authenticate_user(email: str, password: str, *, client_ip: str, users: UserRepository, store: CounterStore) -> User | None. It returns the user for a correct password and None for a wrong password or an unknown email, logs each failed attempt with logging.getLogger(__name__).info including client_ip, and does not use store. No AccountLockedError exists yet.

app/config.py uses only the standard library: a frozen dataclass Settings read from os.environ (redis_url, token_secret, token_ttl_seconds) with development defaults, and a module-level settings object, so it imports with no environment variables set. Every module under app/services/ imports only the standard library and other app/services/ modules (never fastapi, redis, or app/db), so python3 -m pytest runs in the image.

app/routers/auth.py: an APIRouter with POST /auth/login taking a JSON body with email and password. It calls authenticate_user with client_ip=request.client.host, users from Depends(get_user_repository), and store from Depends(get_counter_store) (both in app/dependencies.py; get_counter_store returns RedisCounterStore(settings.redis_url)), raises HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid email or password") when the result is None, and otherwise returns a token from app/services/tokens.py. app/main.py creates the app and includes the router. A SQLAlchemy-backed user repository in app/db/users.py serves production.

pyproject.toml declares fastapi, uvicorn, sqlalchemy, and redis, a dev dependency group with pytest and ruff, and [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths = ["tests"]. tests/unit/ has test_auth_service.py (a correct password returns the user; a wrong password and an unknown email return None), test_counter_store.py (InMemoryCounterStore with a fake clock), and test_passwords.py; all pass with python3 -m pytest. No test covers lockout. README.md gives setup with uv, running with uvicorn, and testing with uv run pytest.

Technical design (FEATURE mode): exactly the points in the prompt: AccountLockedError; counting in the CounterStore that authenticate_user receives; the two settings and the two keyword-only parameters the router fills from them, so app/services/ keeps its import boundary; a CounterStoreError propagating out of authenticate_user, which the router answers with 503; the 429 mapping; and that how failed attempts are counted in the store, including whether a successful login resets them, is an implementation detail for the developer. The scope leaves that reset to the design, and its non-goals include changes to password hashing and to login response timing. It does not mention unknown emails or client addresses, and it does not say how the 15-minute window is measured.
